title: Proton's chief executive cancelled the AI re-interviews. He said the push continues
friendlyTitle: Proton's chief executive cancelled the AI re-interviews. He said the push continues
summary: On 30 October, 404 Media reported that Proton chief executive Andy Yen cancelled a round of near company-wide re-interviews that would have asked staff how they use AI, with job loss as the implied stake. The cancellation followed 404 Media's report the day before on Yen pushing AI use, including a Slack line calling caution 'loser thinking.' Yen told an all-hands that there had been a communication failure, and that he is still going to push. He said a reorganization next month will not mean jobs lost to AI. Employees told 404 Media that what the interviews would have measured is set to become part of performance reviews.

This followed 404 Media's report the day before on Yen pushing AI use, including a staff-chat line that called caution 'loser thinking.' Yen told a company meeting that he had failed to communicate, and that he is still going to push. He said a reorganization next month will not mean jobs lost because of AI. Employees told 404 Media that what the interviews would have measured is set to become part of performance reviews.
whyItMatters: If you pay Proton for privacy tools, the interviews are cancelled and the direction is not. Yen said there will be no job losses from AI. Staff who spoke to 404 Media said that is not the same as a change in what the company is building, or in how AI use will be scored. The piece is useful as a workplace document, not as a product changelog.
